workflow.title: Review a Mac cleaner's junk list without treating every large file as disposable
workflow.primaryIntent: Use the documented CleanGeeker category/file review workflow to distinguish disposable cache candidates from personal attachments, duplicates and archives.
workflow.leadDirection: Inspect categories and specific files before approving removal; a vendor's junk label is not evidence that a file is expendable.
sections: Start with the documented category and file list, not a one-click result
Separate cache candidates from originals, duplicates and attachments
Record backups, rebuild/download costs and confirmation scope
Check whether the same category grows again rather than claiming a speedup
Choose documented toolkit features or preview investigation based on the actual job
workflow.interactionPass: Hand off a non-mutating decision checklist: known owner, reproducible cache, backed-up original, unknown location. Unknown/original routes to keep/review; size never grants deletion permission. No scanner or savings estimator implied.
workflow.visualPlan: Cleared real competitor category/file screenshot directly after lead, current-source Breathing Room Space example preview later. Rights gate currently blocks the competitor image.
workflow.limitations: No terminal cleanup commands or hands-on outcomes; independently source macOS/cache guidance before writing procedural advice; never instruct erasure or bypass Gatekeeper.
